elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Tertiary Education Access Rates (%) by Expenditure Quintiles, 2006-2018
elements.content:
Chart type: Line chart
Axis titles: x-axis: Year (no label printed), y-axis: Access rate (%), unlabeled explicitly, scale 0 to 80
Legend: Poorest Quintile, 2nd Poorest, Middle, 2nd Richest, Richest Quintile

Data points:
Poorest Quintile:
- 2006: ≈ 1%
- 2010: ≈ 2%
- 2014: ≈ 3%
- 2018: ≈ 5%

2nd Poorest:
- 2006: ≈ 3%
- 2010: ≈ 7%
- 2014: ≈ 10%
- 2018: ≈ 15%

Middle:
- 2006: ≈ 8%
- 2010: ≈ 18%
- 2014: ≈ 26%
- 2018: ≈ 31%

2nd Richest:
- 2006: ≈ 16%
- 2010: ≈ 28%
- 2014: ≈ 41%
- 2018: ≈ 45%

Richest Quintile:
- 2006: ≈ 38%
- 2010: ≈ 54%
- 2014: ≈ 64%
- 2018: ≈ 72%

Factual comparisons:
- The Richest Quintile consistently maintained the highest access rate across all years, rising from around 38% in 2006 to 72% in 2018.
- The Poorest Quintile had the lowest access rate throughout the period, remaining below 5%.
- The gap between the richest and poorest quintiles widened significantly from around 37 percentage points in 2006 to 67 percentage points in 2018.

Source: Authors' estimates using VHLSS (2006-2018).

elements.content:
Chart type: 100% stacked area chart
Axis titles: x-axis: Year (no label printed), y-axis: Share (%), unlabeled explicitly, scale 0 to 100
Legend: Poorest Quintile, 2nd Poorest, Middle, 2nd Richest, Richest Quintile

Data points (estimated shares of total opportunities):
2006:
- Poorest Quintile: ≈ 2%
- 2nd Poorest: ≈ 5%
- Middle: ≈ 13%
- 2nd Richest: ≈ 30%
- Richest Quintile: ≈ 50%

2010:
- Poorest Quintile: ≈ 1.5%
- 2nd Poorest: ≈ 5.5%
- Middle: ≈ 16%
- 2nd Richest: ≈ 28%
- Richest Quintile: ≈ 49%

2014:
- Poorest Quintile: ≈ 1.5%
- 2nd Poorest: ≈ 5.5%
- Middle: ≈ 16%
- 2nd Richest: ≈ 28%
- Richest Quintile: ≈ 49%

2018:
- Poorest Quintile: ≈ 1.5%
- 2nd Poorest: ≈ 5.5%
- Middle: ≈ 17%
- 2nd Richest: ≈ 27%
- Richest Quintile: ≈ 49%

Factual comparisons:
- The top two expenditure quintiles accounted for the vast majority (nearly 80%) of tertiary education opportunities throughout 2006–2018.
- The bottom two quintiles combined represented less than 10% of total tertiary education opportunities across the entire period.
- The share held by the Richest Quintile remained dominant and stable at approximately 49–50%.

Source: Authors' estimates using VHLSS (2006-2018).
